items.caption:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says he gets made fun of almost every day because Claude's biology safeguards are too strong, and he would rather have that than learn someone used the model to kill people.

He says he feels both sides of it, and that this shouldn't be the responsibility of one company or even one government.

Who should be responsible for AI safety: the companies or governments?

Source: CBS Sunday Morning, Extended interview: Dario Amodei (CEO of Anthropic). Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=hQR_VJF6ukk

items.caption:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says that for too long, the AI industry lied to people about the risks.

He also says the upside is real: every week he gets an email from someone saying Claude diagnosed a disease their doctors had missed. His point is that it starts with telling the truth.

Do you trust what AI companies tell you about the risks?

Mark Zuckerberg says that when he told the team 10 years ago they were going to build these glasses, people weren't sure they could.

He says it all got miniaturized into a normal looking pair, and he expects them to get cheaper, higher quality, smaller and more stylish over time.

Would you wear holographic glasses every day?

items.caption:
Mark Zuckerberg says the average person would like to have 10 friends and has two or three.

He says glasses that let you be present with people far away aren't replacing a better physical connection. His example: not less time with his wife, but more time with his sister who lives across the country.

Does tech bring you closer to people, or further away?

Source: Cleo Abram, The Future Mark Zuckerberg Is Trying To Build. Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=oX7OduG1YmI

items.caption:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says the pace of AI is a warning sign that we need to slow down.

He doesn't call it a reason to panic or to shut it all down. He says we're on the bend of the curve, where it starts to get steeper, and that safeguards have to keep up with the technology.

Should AI labs slow down, or is speed the safer bet?
